comments.note: Reviewed all 52 exported method JSDoc blocks. Structure is uniform and clean: description → @param → @returns → @throws in every block. The shared request() helper's rejection shape `{ code, message }` is clearly the source of truth, and the @throws tag accurately describes the runtime contract. No redundancies, no gaps.

Function count verification: 58 total `function (` occurrences in the file — 52 exported API methods + 2 private helpers (request, buildQueryString) + 1 IIFE wrapper + 3 inline .then(function (data)) callbacks. The 52 @throws count matches the 52 exported methods exactly.

Notable positive: buildQueryString's docstring explicitly explains why `0` and `false` are NOT omitted (only undefined and empty-string are filtered), and getRunLogEntries has an inline comment explaining why it uses a manual ternary instead of buildQueryString for the afterLine=0 edge case. This level of in-code rationale for non-obvious design decisions is commendable and should be maintained as a standard.

[documentation-forward] The @typedef blocks (GuiConfig, InsightEntry, ServerInfo, ServerVersions, DialogueBlock) are thorough and well-placed within the IIFE scope. No documentation gaps in the @throws coverage itself, but if a top-level README or JSDoc-generated API surface document exists for the GUI public JS modules, it should call out that ALL public API methods throw `{ code: string, message: string }` as a module-level contract — callers should catch this shape at every call site.
